title: Versioned Ledger Migration and Isolated PostgreSQL Verification
objective: Create the formal versioned Ledger SQL migration mechanism, realize the frozen eleven-table ORM shape, integrate fresh install, and verify up, parity, constraints, rollback, reapply, and cleanup in isolated PostgreSQL.
scope: Explicit versioned PostgreSQL SQL, manifest, exact-byte checksums, migration history, ordered runner, transactions, advisory lock, guarded down, and fresh-install invocation.
Database-free contract tests plus disposable PostgreSQL 15 catalog parity, valid/invalid data, idempotency, checksum drift, rollback atomicity, reapply, and cleanup.
Migration contract, bounded Project Memory and context-schema updates, full relevant regression, immutable Implementation Run, and one local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No PostgreSQL Repository, Repository adapter, business Session, Unit of Work, Manifest Parser, Indexer, identity resolver, Git consistency service, API, or UI.

No production database operation, broad privilege policy, new dependency, lockfile, accepted ADR, runtime configuration, Factor Lab, TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation, Registry, LightGBM, or Qlib change.
No push, amend, rebase, reset, stash, clean, or secret output.

tests_executed.scope: Manifest, exact checksums, ordering, pairing, path safety, UTF-8, SQL scope, plan, down gate, safe argv, and static ORM inventory.

tests_executed.command: Four initial opt-in PostgreSQL integration iterations
tests_executed.scope: Exercise the new disposable PostgreSQL harness and catalog queries.
tests_executed.evidence: The test harness exposed one runner-vs-psql database flag mismatch, one pg_catalog char cast ambiguity, and two concatenated-select ORDER BY errors; each harness defect was corrected before the successful full lifecycle.

tests_executed.scope: Disposable PostgreSQL 15 initial state, up, parity, valid/18 invalid writes, RESTRICT, idempotency, drift, failed-down atomicity, down, reapply, and cleanup.
tests_executed.evidence: The complete lifecycle passed in 2.61 seconds and the random-named no-volume container was removed.

tests_executed.command: First full relevant Ledger and Context regression after migration implementation
tests_executed.scope: Domain, Repository contract, ORM, Mapper, migration, PostgreSQL, and Context behavior.
tests_executed.evidence: Three stale pre-A2b guards still prohibited a migration or required A2b as the next task; they were updated to validate migration checksums while retaining Repository/API scope guards. 247 subtests passed.

tests_executed.command: QM2_LEDGER_POSTGRES_INTEGRATION=1 Existing SQLAlchemy Python -m pytest --no-cov -q all relevant Ledger Domain/Repository/ORM/Mapper/Migration/PostgreSQL/Context files
tests_executed.scope: Full task-relevant regression including a fresh disposable PostgreSQL lifecycle.
tests_executed.evidence: Final regression passed 336 tests and 247 subtests in 2.81 seconds.

tests_executed.scope: Context schemas/paths/ADRs, Ledger contracts/mappings/migration checksums, Run pairs, exact A3 handoff, and official Factor Lab path.
tests_executed.evidence: Bounded bootstrap validator returned passed with 35 named checks.

tests_executed.command: python3 JSON parse, Python compile, migration validate/plan, git diff --check, scope, Docker cleanup, and Factor Lab cleanliness guards
tests_executed.scope: Machine documents, changed Python syntax, migration bytes, whitespace/scope, no leftover container, and read-only donor.
tests_executed.evidence: All final structural and workspace guards passed; no dependency or lockfile changed.

known_limitations: No PostgreSQL Repository, business Session/Unit of Work, Manifest Parser/Indexer, identity resolver, Git consistency service, API, or UI exists.
No production database has been migrated; production execution-role/schema privilege policy is not frozen.
CI scheduling for the opt-in Docker PostgreSQL integration test is not configured.
Real PostgreSQL 15 parity used SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 expectations; pinned SQLAlchemy 2.0.25 parity remains unconfirmed.
Mapper and technical identity versions are not business-table columns, and database-level Repository concurrency behavior is unverified.
unresolved_questions: Which production execution role will own or receive least-privilege access to quantmind2?
How will CI provide and schedule Docker or isolated PostgreSQL integration capability?
How will the PostgreSQL Repository implement optimistic versions, graph conflicts, atomic batch behavior, and transaction ownership without committing internally?
How will a future Indexer bind logical repository identity and persist Mapper/identity versions?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No production database was changed. For an explicitly migrated non-production database whose latest matching version is 0001, run down with --allow-destructive before reverting if schema removal is intended.
security_impact: Migration subprocesses use explicit argv and SQL stdin; passwords remain in PGPASSWORD and are redacted from errors. No database URL, password, broad grant, role change, production connection, or secret is stored or printed.
data_lineage_impact: Git remains the Implementation Run authority and PostgreSQL remains a derived query index. _schema_migrations records database shape only. Disposable test rows were destroyed; no research or production data changed.
